contract: ../../doc/implementation/node-selection.md — HA-DESIGN-SEL-001/r1; real DOM hierarchy, exact node inspection and a separate explicit class action.

accessibility.evidence: Existing axe A/AA checks pass with the class actions. Real browser Enter/Space paths distinguish class buttons from tree rows; native buttons have French names and focus styles. Node labels and ARIA hierarchy remain intact.

responsive.evidence: Node and class browser paths verify no horizontal overflow at 320 and 1440 pixels. Actual Chromium individual and group captures were inspected: node identifiers and separate class actions wrap within the bounded structure panel.

loading.reason: The local fixture mounts synchronously without remote project loading.

empty.evidence: Startup has no selected rows or overlays while recorded group/ID preview values remain visible. No object, key or ID is created by inspection.

error.evidence: Literal punctuation classes remain inspectable. Integration tests refuse unsupported animated targets and distinguish a literal a.b token from classes a and b without modifying keys or history.

partial.evidence: Explicit group selection preserves the divergent original margin diagnostic. Returning to a node enables individual margin inspection.

success.evidence: Mouse and keyboard journeys cover node to class to node, exact ID association, first individual ID edit, sibling preview retention and undo. Selection events and persistent-document separation are tested.

permission.reason: No account or production permission operation is exposed by this local demo.

All four real button nodes remain in their parent hierarchy. Only button#button-1 is selected; class links are distinct and the property view is individual.
Explicit class selection fits the stacked workbench and retains the group selection state and simulated two-key count.
The .button action highlights four existing sibling rows and four scene elements without inventing a hierarchy group. Inspector shows the explicit class target and mixed-margin diagnostic.
